---
title: "Reproducibility and build"
---

## What can be reproduced now

This repository builds an explanatory website from plain Quarto sources without downloading posting data or executing analytical notebooks. The two downloadable metric tables are transcriptions of Tables IV and V. The source PDF remains at the user-supplied local location and is not redistributed by the site.

```bash
quarto render
python scripts/verify_site.py
```

The output is `_site/index.html`. These commands finish without starting a local server. Quarto 1.11.1 was available during construction. The site uses no Python analysis dependencies; the verification script uses Python's standard library.

## Word report

`final_report.qmd` synthesizes the reconstruction and course-extension limitations. Render it independently:

```bash
quarto render final_report.qmd --to docx
```

The report is a reconstruction report, not a completed empirical career evaluation. Rebuild it when the underlying evidence changes.

## New empirical study

An exact replication needs the original Jobfeed records, legacy labels, employer and title normalization resources, manual review decisions and model configurations. Jobs_2026 would support a new adaptation, not automatically an exact recreation of the 2017 sample.

The course guides require analytical work on the assigned AWS EC2 environment. Local website construction here does not constitute an EC2 analysis. Use the course's setup instructions there, retain the actual environment versions and keep credentials in an ignored `.env` file. Do not copy API keys into notebooks or rendered pages.

## Publishing

The repository is configured to produce a static `_site` directory suitable for hosting. Public deployment has not been performed. Publishing requires an identified GitHub repository and Pages configuration; verify the live URL and navigation after deployment before marking the course publication requirement complete.
